N° 09Bilingual study platform: notes, transcription and active recall2026

How to use Mosaic

For learners in school, university or professional training who attend classes, read chapters and prepare exams, in English or French, on a computer or a phone.

Open Mosaic ↗Platform detailsContact

Guided tourReal screens

Plays automatically. Use the dots or arrows to move, Pause to stop.

01

Getting started

1

Go to mosaic-learn.vercel.app. FR or EN at the top switches the language at any time.

2

To see everything first, open the guided demo and press Start the guided demo: a sample notebook loads and 30 steps show each feature.

3

Notes is your notebook. On a phone, the bottom bar holds Notes, Learn, the + button, Review and More.

4

Record class, at the top, records a lesson; the + button or New from… brings in a file, a video, a photo, a YouTube video, a web page or a topic.

5

Mentor, at the top, answers questions about the page you are on and proposes flashcards or a plan that you confirm.

02

Features

01

The notebook home

One card to bring anything: a class, a PDF, a video, a photo of your notebook. Below it: the cards to review today, the tasks due, and the note to pick up where you left off.

STEPS

  1. Press New note to write
  2. Or Upload file, Record class or Video or audio
  3. Open the note under Pick up where you left off
02

Video or audio, transcribed on the device

Drop a lecture, a class recording or a meeting. Mosaic keeps the original on your device, transcribes it there, finds the chapters and writes the note with timestamps. On a computer, Chrome and Edge can also record the sound of a meeting tab.

STEPS

  1. Choose Video or audio
  2. Press Choose a video or audio file
  3. Or Record a meeting tab and tell the others
03

The + button on a phone

One sheet for every way in: a new note, a class to record, a file, a video or audio, a scan, photos, a web page, YouTube, pasted text, a topic, or an animation in Visual Studio.

STEPS

  1. Tap + in the middle of the bottom bar
  2. Pick a source
  3. The bar slides away while you type
04

The transcript

Every segment is timestamped, searchable and editable, and Copy all takes the whole text. The recording stays attached to the note.

STEPS

  1. Open Transcript under the title
  2. Search a word
  3. Correct a segment
05

The note Claude writes

The note reads like a good handout: in short, plain words, an analogy, a roadmap, chapters with times, the explanation, a worked example, words to explain, traps and practice. Equations render as mathematics, and every part can be edited.

STEPS

  1. Read the roadmap first
  2. Press a chapter time to replay that moment
  3. Edit it like any document
06

A rich editor

Insert, or a slash, adds tasks with a due date, calendar events, links, links to other notes, tables, images, video, audio, sketches, code, equations, flashcards, quizzes, diagrams and interactive visualizations. Everything saves as you type.

STEPS

  1. Press Insert or type /
  2. Filter by typing a word
  3. Pick a block
07

Teach it back

Explain the idea without your notes. Mosaic checks your explanation against the key ideas, shows what is missing or not quite right, and lists the words you used without explaining them.

STEPS

  1. Open the Teach it back tab
  2. Write or dictate your explanation
  3. Press Check my explanation
08

Quiz, flashcards and mock exam

Questions built from the note, with an explanation for every answer; flashcards scheduled by spaced repetition so they come back just before you forget; and a mock exam to finish.

STEPS

  1. Open Quiz, Flashcards or Mock exam
  2. Answer before reading the explanation
  3. Come back through Review
09

Visual Studio

Visualize turns a note, a selection, a PDF passage or a transcript into an animated, interactive explanation, checked before it plays, with narration, steps, a knowledge check and sources. Here, a laptop gets its address through DHCP, message by message.

STEPS

  1. Press Visualize on a note or a selection
  2. Play it or step through it
  3. Refine it, then Save
10

Lessons with interactive models

Flagship lessons open on tabs: Learn, See it, Practise, Explain, Test, Review and Deep study. In See it, sliders change a, b and c and the parabola moves with them.

STEPS

  1. Open Learn and pick a subject
  2. Open a lesson
  3. Try See it, then Test
11

Documents and the PDF viewer

PDF, Word, PowerPoint, EPUB and text are processed on your device; scanned pages are read by the AI. The viewer has search, highlights and notes kept in Mosaic, sending to a note, and Visualize.

STEPS

  1. Upload a PDF from the notebook
  2. Highlight a passage
  3. Send it to the note or visualize it
12

Tasks and calendar

Tasks inside notes or on their own, with due dates, priority and repeats; a month and day calendar with study-plan sessions; and an export to any calendar app.

STEPS

  1. Open Calendar
  2. Press New event or add a task in a note
  3. Export .ics for your calendar app
13

The guided demo

A sample notebook (a narrated lecture video with its transcript, a PDF chapter, a photo of handwritten notes, a web article, a revision plan, animations, tasks and flashcards) and a 30-step walkthrough that highlights each feature without blocking it, with Show me actions. Removing the sample leaves your own notes untouched.

STEPS

  1. Open the guided demo
  2. Press Start the guided demo, then Next
  3. Remove the sample notebook when you are done
03Tips
  • Record the class, then do Teach it back the same evening: explaining without notes shows what you did not understand while the lecture is still fresh.
  • To show Mosaic to someone, send the guided demo link: the walkthrough starts directly on a sample notebook, and their own notes are never touched.
  • On a phone, install Mosaic from More: it then opens straight on the notebook.
  • Split recordings longer than about two hours before importing them.
04FAQ
Is it free?

Every feature is open for 7 days, without a card. The paid plans are built, but payments are not switched on yet.

Are my recordings uploaded?

No. Audio and video are transcribed on your device and the originals stay there. To write the note, the transcript and a few still frames are sent to Claude.

Which languages?

English and French, for the interface and the notes. French transcription has not yet been measured on real lectures.

Does every subject have lessons?

Not yet. The flagship lessons are complete; most subjects have their concepts and pathway but no lesson yet. Your own notes work on any subject.

Do I need an account?

No. Notes live in your browser. Signing in by email link is optional; note backup and read-only sharing are being switched on.
